objective: A quantity price tier is not applied at exactly its minimum quantity. With a tier "from 10 units on, 900 per unit" and a base price of 1000, ten units are priced at 1000 and only eleven units get 900. A tier applies from its minimum quantity on (the minimum itself included). When several tiers are reached, the one with the largest minimum quantity applies, whatever its price; when none is reached, the base price applies.
acceptance: With the tier (10 units, 900) and base price 1000, 9 units cost 1000 each, 10, 11 and 1000 units cost 900 each
With tiers (10, 900), (50, 800) and (200, 700) and base price 1000: 1 and 9 units cost 1000, 10, 11 and 49 cost 900, 50, 51 and 199 cost 800, 200 and 201 cost 700
The result does not depend on the order of the tiers or on whether they are given as a list, a tuple or a generator
With tiers (10, 900) and (20, 950) and base price 1000: 10 and 19 units cost 900, 20 and 25 units cost 950 (the largest minimum reached wins, even when its price is higher)
A tier starting at 1 unit applies to a single unit: tier (1, 950) gives 950 for 1 unit; with tiers (1, 950) and (5, 900), 2 units cost 950 and 5 units cost 900
Without tiers, with an empty tier list, or when the quantity is below every minimum, the base price is used; a free tier (10, 0) on a base price of 0 gives 0
